Water Damage Restoration for Car Interiors

Wet carpet does not dry on its own in a closed car. It sours, grows mildew and works into the padding underneath. The faster the water is extracted and the interior properly dried, the more we can save.

What we do for a wet interior

  • Find the source: an open window, a sunroof drain, a door or windshield seal, a clogged cowl. Restoring the interior without fixing the leak just repeats the problem.
  • Extract: hot-water extraction pulls water out of carpet, padding and seat foam. Where needed we lift carpet to reach the padding and the floor pan.
  • Dry: forced airflow and, where appropriate, removal of saturated padding. We check moisture before we call it done.
  • Treat: shampoo, antimicrobial treatment and odor removal so the mildew smell does not come back. Ozone treatment is used where it is appropriate for the vehicle.
  • Replace: when carpet or padding is too far gone to save, we replace it. We already do soaked-carpet and upholstery replacement as part of our interior work.

What to do right now

  1. Get the water out of the car as soon as you can: towels, a wet-dry vacuum, open doors in the shade. Every day the carpet stays wet makes it harder to save.
  2. Photograph the waterline and every wet area before anything is removed.
  3. Do not start the car if water reached the dash, the seats’ electrical connectors or the floor-mounted modules. Have it looked at first.
  4. Send us the photos and tell us how high the water got. That one detail changes what we recommend.

Repairable water damage vs. a flooded vehicle

These are different situations, and we will tell you which one you have.

  • Repairable: rain through an open window or sunroof, a leaking seal, a spilled cooler, a wet floorboard from a clogged drain. The interior is saved with extraction, drying and treatment, sometimes with new carpet or padding.
  • Flooded: water above the seat bottoms, water in the dash or electrical modules, standing water for days, or any saltwater or sewage contamination. Electrical and corrosion problems show up for months. This is usually a conversation with your insurer about the vehicle’s value, and we will not sell you an interior restoration on a car that should be totaled.

Mildew can start within a day or two in a closed, warm car. If the interior is wet, treat it as urgent.

Water damage and insurance

Flood and water damage from storms is typically handled under comprehensive coverage. Water that got in because a window was left open may be treated differently by some insurers, and a slow leak from a worn seal is usually considered maintenance. Coverage, and what your deductible is, are always your insurance company’s decision, never ours.

We don’t bill your insurance company for you: you receive a written, itemized estimate and photos you can submit with your claim, and we work from the estimate once you decide to proceed. If the vehicle may be a total loss, we will tell you that before you spend money on an estimate you will not use.

Questions people ask

Can a water-damaged car interior be saved?

Usually yes when the water came from rain, a leak or a spill and is dealt with quickly. Carpet, padding and seats can be extracted, dried and treated, or replaced if needed. A vehicle that was flooded above the seats or had water in the electronics is a different situation, and we will tell you if that is the case.

How quickly does mildew start?

In a closed car in Texas heat, often within one to two days. The sooner the interior is extracted and dried, the less treatment it needs and the more likely the original carpet can be saved.

Do you fix the leak too?

We find where the water came in and clear drains and simple seal issues as part of the job. Body seam or windshield-seal repairs may need a glass or body shop, and we will tell you if that is what we find.

Will insurance cover water damage to my car?

Storm and flood damage is typically a comprehensive claim, while damage from a window left open or a worn seal may be handled differently. Your insurer decides. We provide the written estimate and photos you need to ask the question.

Is ozone treatment safe for my car?

Used correctly and in the right situations it is an effective odor treatment. We decide whether it is appropriate for your vehicle and materials, and we never use it as a substitute for actually drying and cleaning the interior.
